A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of interaction-based learning of intuitive physics. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original GRPO/SFT training experiments, cross-task evaluations, representation probes and ablations on simulated and real block-tower images.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds triplet-task, additional model-family and prompt-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The triplet condition extends the input/action interface to three images interleaved with two supplied actions, followed by a predicted displacement with wider limits and downward movement allowed (Section 4.5.3; Appendix A.5). The GRPO/SFT objectives, reward functions and core adaptation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds a temporal-context version of the x-y side-block task using three successive states and intervening actions. This extends the input scenario within the existing block-tower domain; the original top-block, side-block and real-image coverage remains.

E2.justification: The training comparators remain GRPO, SFT and the existing GSPO variants, with retained base-model, chance and human references. The added Llama and Gemma experiments apply the existing GRPO/SFT comparison to additional backbones.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation through single/triplet transfer tests, Llama-3.2-11B and Gemma-3-12B configurations, legal-answer-only binary accuracy, and five prompt variants tested on the same 1,000 images (Sections 4.5.3, A.2, A.8 and A.11). Gemma's training task is inconsistently labeled in Figure 18. Newly stated original dataset sizes are documentation, not evidence of changed splits.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to temporal context, model family, prompt wording and malformed responses. These address several alternative explanations for poor transfer beyond v1's retained rank, reasoning-length, vision-encoder, training-duration and multitask ablations.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly displays error bars for the retained single-image x-y result, previously presented without uncertainty in Figure 2 and the result tables. Their construction is unspecified. Existing 95% confidence intervals for real-image evaluations and 10-fold probe validation remain, with no newly reported training-run or seed counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds triplet-transfer, Llama/Gemma and prompt-sensitivity outcomes. Appendix A.2 reports 0.74 legal-answer accuracy for GRPO x-y-to-binary transfer, excluding 5,770 invalid responses, alongside the retained all-response reward of -0.264. The x-y diagonal table entries change from 19.868/15.839 for GRPO/SFT in v1 to 17.313/19.86 in v2, aligning with the existing narrative rather than demonstrating rerun improvements.

T1.justification: The GRPO and SFT losses, advantage expression, adapter formulation and reward mathematics are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2's conceptual explanations introduce no new formal theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that interaction-based post-training improves within-task performance without reliably producing transferable physical intuitions or a general advantage over SFT. The hypotheses and principal contribution remain; added experiments provide further evidence.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies conclusions by constrained training settings and quantized PEFT, proposing full fine-tuning checks. Its discussion develops retained multitask and probing findings into suggestions for curricula and auxiliary physical-variable objectives. Section 4.5.3 also explains the lack of observed action consequences in the original setup.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies 10,000 training and 10,000 separate evaluation images per original task and one image per training step. Appendices add the complete triplet dialogue, expanded action ranges, prompt variants and the 1,000-image sensitivity-test size. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning: it distinguishes Han et al.'s stability fine-tuning study from the present cross-task generalization question, adds physical-plausibility and world-model research, and qualifies earlier visual-failure framing with recent multi-object and counting work. Additional developmental-physics and quantization literature supports the introduction and limitations.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites to the introduction, related work, task descriptions and discussion while retaining the main narrative structure. It swaps the appendix training-log and prompt sections, adds explicit Limitations and Impact Statement text, and updates title capitalization, author markers and publication information.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial visual material for triplet examples and transfer, Llama/Gemma evaluations and prompt sensitivity (Figures 4, 7, 17, 18 and 26). It merges the earlier separate appendix result tables into main-text Table 1, adds legal-answer tables and redraws Figure 1. Most earlier plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The added model-family, temporal-context and prompt checks strengthen the evidence, while legal-answer accuracy and dataset/prompt documentation improve interpretability and reproducibility. These gains are bounded: the triplet supplies earlier actions rather than establishing autonomous multistep interaction, and reporting inconsistencies remain, including Section 4.2's 0.624 versus Table 1's 0.788 and Figure 18's conflicting Gemma training labels.
